subject: zoology
question_text: List out eight characteristics that help distinguish a fish from the other vertebrates.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.39, SAQ 35). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Habitat and scales
steps.margin_note: Two characters here. Eight are asked, so plan two per mark.
lines: 1) Fishes are aquatic, ectothermal (cold
blooded), scaly vertebrates.
2) The scales are mesodermal in origin. In some
fishes they are modified into shields or into
spines.
steps.why: The scales of a fish come from the mesoderm, unlike the ectodermal scales of a reptile, so the origin is the fact that separates the two and is worth writing.
common_mistakes: Writing that fish scales are ectodermal. They are mesodermal; reptile scales are ectodermal.
Calling fishes warm blooded. They are ectothermal.
steps.memory_tip: Water, cold blood, scales from the middle layer: the first three words of the answer.

steps.label: Vertebrae and fins
steps.margin_note: Name all five fins. Half marks are lost by writing only fins are present.
lines: 3) The vertebrae are amphicoelous: the centrum
is hollowed on both faces.
4) Fins are present and are used for
locomotion.
5) The fins are of two kinds. Paired fins are
the pectoral and the pelvic. Median fins are
the dorsal, the caudal and the anal.
steps.why: Fins are the character a student can see, so the answer separates them into paired and median and names all five, which is what the examiner counts.
common_mistakes: Writing that all fins are paired. The dorsal, caudal and anal fins are median and single.
Calling the vertebrae procoelous. Fish vertebrae are amphicoelous, hollow on both faces.
steps.memory_tip: Two paired, three median: pectoral and pelvic in pairs, dorsal, caudal and anal single.

steps.label: Gills and gill slits
steps.margin_note: Two characters. The operculum contrast is a cheap extra line that reads well.
lines: 6) Gills are the respiratory organs.
7) The gill slits are open in cartilaginous
fishes.
In bony fishes they are covered by a bony flap
called the operculum.
steps.why: Gills are what make a fish a fish, and the open or covered slit is the one line that also separates the two classes of fishes inside the group.
common_mistakes: Writing that all fishes have an operculum. Cartilaginous fishes have open gill slits.
Saying fishes breathe through lungs. Gills are the respiratory organs.
steps.memory_tip: Shark slits are open to the water; a bony fish keeps its slits under a lid.

steps.label: The heart
steps.margin_note: Close with the heart. Both names with both reasons make this the strongest mark.
lines: 8) The heart is ventral in position and two
chambered, with one auricle and one ventricle.
It is called a branchial heart, because it
pumps blood directly to the gills.
It is also called a venous heart, because it
holds only deoxygenated blood.
steps.why: The two names of the fish heart come from two different facts, where the blood goes and what kind of blood it is, so both names need their own reason.
common_mistakes: Writing three chambers. The fish heart has only two.
Giving one name without its reason. Branchial is for the gills, venous is for the blood.
steps.memory_tip: One name for the destination (branchial, to the gills), one for the contents (venous).

insider_note: Eight characters are asked and four marks are given, so write them numbered 1 to 8 — an examiner counting a numbered list awards faster than one reading a paragraph.
